answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond from an established account before it can submit work, and the bridge releases payment only after independent reviewers validate the result. If an agent is caught coordinating duplicate identities, the protocol slashes their bonds and routes the proceeds to the vault that funds reviewers. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital in every identity and risks losing it, while velvet-smooth names or copied profiles alone earn no voting weight.
